svg.text: A home that mostly runs itself
one free, open-source brain · any brand · cheap DIY parts · repurposed tech · no ecosystem lock-in
tracks up to 9 people, each to the spot,
even when they’re sitting perfectly still,
then lights, music & more adapt to who’s
where, the time, the temperature, when
they got home and what others are doing
even things I’d once have called broken,
each repurposed for one useful job:
old laptop → my private cloud & Zigbee hub
end-of-life QNAP NAS → Unraid media server
local control first; the cloud only where
a brand gives no other choice
can be hooked in cheaply too
a dozen apps → one home that cooperates
Like a creepy smart home Santa, it knows
when I’m sleeping and it knows when I’m awake.
It’s tuned to what I want by where I am,
the day, the time and what I’m doing:
lights, music, alarms and the door lock
just happen. Alerts find me on
runs at home; most of it works offline
a backup clone of the brain stands by,
ready to take over in about 5 minutes
daily backups to my NAS and the cloud
One remote for the whole home
A custom app I designed from the ground up, running on an
affordable Android remote (Astrion HA100). Touch screen,
physical buttons or voice (“hey Pikachu”): TV, music,
lights, scenes and alerts in one hand.
Swap any brand in or out — the brain, the automations and the way I live with it stay the same.
